hook.text: Instagram was just a photo filter app at launch. It was useful even if nobody else was on it.

buildup.text: Single-player mode means the product has standalone value before network effects kick in.

discovery.text: OpenTable gave restaurants a free reservation system. Useful alone, but magical once diners joined.

twist.text: Most failed platforms skipped single-player mode. They needed both sides from day one—an impossible ask.

climax.text: Single-player mode is the safest way to solve the chicken-and-egg problem. Deliver value immediately.

punchline.text: Make it useful for one person first. The network comes later.

details.summary: Single-player mode is a platform launch strategy where the product provides standalone value to individual users before any network effects kick in. Instagram was useful as a photo filter app before it became a social network. This approach solves the cold start problem organically.
details.whyItMatters: Single-player mode is one of the most effective cold start solutions because it acquires users on product merit alone. Once a critical mass of single-player users exists, the platform activates multi-player features that ignite network effects.
takeaways: Standalone utility attracts users before network effects exist
Once enough single-player users accumulate, social features are activated
This approach reduces the capital needed to bootstrap network effects

faq.question: What are good examples of successful single-player mode strategies?
faq.answer: Instagram launched as a photo filter tool. OpenTable first sold reservation management software to individual restaurants. Yelp started with user reviews that had standalone search value. Each product was useful to individuals before the network dimension emerged.

faq.question: What makes a good single-player mode product?
faq.answer: It must solve a real problem well enough that users adopt it without any network. It should naturally generate data or content that becomes the foundation for network features. The transition from single to multi-player must feel like an enhancement, not a pivot.
